The provision allowing a split of one-third of a legislature party was removed
questions.why: The 91st Amendment removed the one-third split exception, so only a merger of two-thirds of the legislature party protects members from disqualification.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: In Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992) the Supreme Court held that
opts: the Tenth Schedule is invalid because it violates the freedom of speech of legislators
the Speaker’s decision on disqualification is final and cannot be questioned in any court
the decision of the Speaker on disqualification is subject to judicial review
the Election Commission alone is empowered to decide on all disqualification petitions
questions.why: The Court upheld the Tenth Schedule but held that the Speaker’s decision is open to judicial review on limited grounds.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the India–Nepal Joint Vision announced in November 2026:
1. India announced a development cooperation package of ₹15,000 crore for Nepal.
2. Kandla and Paradip were added as ports for Nepal’s transit cargo.
3. The 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship was terminated with immediate effect.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: The package and the additional ports were announced. The 1950 Treaty is to be reviewed by mutual consent; it was not terminated.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The motorable bridge between Dharchula in India and Darchula in Nepal is built over which river?
questions.why: The Mahakali, known as the Sharda in India, forms part of the India–Nepal boundary in this section.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, consider the following statements:
1. India became a full member in 2017.
2. Iran became a member in 2023.
3. Its secretariat is located in Moscow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: India joined in 2017 and Iran in 2023. The SCO Secretariat is in Beijing.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The first Civilisational Dialogue Forum of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, held in November 2026, adopted a document known as the
questions.why: The forum at Purana Qila, New Delhi adopted the Indraprastha Communiqué on cultural cooperation and shared heritage.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to securitisation of loans, consider the following statements:
1. A lender sells a pool of loans to a special purpose vehicle that issues securities backed by the repayments.
2. It helps lenders free capital for fresh lending.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Both are correct. Securitisation converts a pool of loans into tradable securities and frees capital for new credit.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Under the Reserve Bank’s final securitisation amendments issued in November 2026, a minimum ticket size per investor is fixed at
questions.why: A minimum ticket size of ₹1 crore applies at issue and on transfer, and covered notes must be held in dematerialised form from 1 April 2027.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: A feature proposed in the Reserve Bank’s draft rules on electronic payment safeguards that blocks outward debits from an account while allowing credits to continue is called a
questions.why: The Stop Switch blocks outward debits while inward credits continue, giving customers a quick way to protect an account.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Green India Mission is one of the missions under which of the following?
opts: National Clean Energy Mission and Innovation Fund
Namami Gange Programme for rivers and wetlands
National Action Plan on Climate Change
questions.why: The Green India Mission is one of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (2008).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: India’s Nationally Determined Contribution includes creating an additional carbon sink of how much by 2030?
opts: 1 to 1.5 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent
2.5 to 3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent
5 to 6 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent
8 to 10 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent
questions.why: India pledged an additional carbon sink of 2.5 to 3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent through additional forest and tree cover by 2030.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the dugong:
1. It is a marine mammal that feeds mainly on seagrass.
2. India’s first Dugong Conservation Reserve was declared in Palk Bay.
3. It is listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Palk Bay Dugong Conservation Reserve in Tamil Nadu was declared in 2022.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Mass nesting of olive ridley turtles on a beach is known as
questions.why: Arribada is the Spanish word for arrival and describes mass nesting, as seen on the Odisha coast.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which one of the following best describes ‘Just Transition’ in climate negotiations?
opts: Support for workers and regions dependent on fossil fuels as the economy shifts to clean energy
A transfer of clean energy technology free of cost to every developing country that formally asks for it
A global fund that pays for the permanent loss of coastal land when the sea level rises over time
A carbon tax that is charged at the border on all goods imported from every country in the world
questions.why: Just Transition covers training, jobs and support for people and places that depend on fossil fuels.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Decisions at the Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC are generally taken by
questions.why: COP decisions are taken by consensus, so objection by even one Party can block a text.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The joint ISRO–CNES satellite mission TRISHNA is intended for
opts: thermal infrared observation of land and water surfaces
deep space observation of distant galaxies and black holes in the universe
navigation and timing signals for aircraft, ships and ground vehicles
communication links for remote villages and mountain regions of the country
questions.why: TRISHNA is a thermal infrared Earth observation mission for water and land surface monitoring, planned in a sun-synchronous orbit.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Which of the following is a joint India–France satellite mission to study the tropical water cycle?
questions.why: Megha-Tropiques (2011) studied the tropical water cycle. SARAL-AltiKa (2013) is a joint ocean altimetry satellite.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: A bacteriophage is a
questions.why: A bacteriophage is a virus that infects bacteria and is used in phage therapy.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about genome language models:
1. They are trained on DNA sequences and learn patterns in them.
2. They can be used to predict the effect of mutations.
3. They pose no biosafety or biosecurity concerns.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: Such models learn from DNA and predict mutation effects, but they raise dual-use concerns, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Indirect calorimetry, as used in a human metabolic chamber, estimates energy expenditure by measuring
opts: body temperature and heart rate measured together over a day
oxygen consumed and carbon dioxide produced
weight gained over a week of regular eating and rest
blood sugar and insulin levels measured after every meal
questions.why: Energy use is inferred from the oxygen a person consumes and the carbon dioxide produced.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The National Industrial Classification (NIC) is used to
opts: classify banks by the size of their assets and deposits
rank the states by their level of industrial output each year
set import duties on industrial goods brought from other countries
group economic activities for statistical purposes
questions.why: NIC is the standard classification of economic activities. The 2026 survey of unincorporated enterprises uses NIC 2025.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which one of the following is excluded from the coverage of the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises?
questions.why: Construction is outside the coverage of the survey of non-agricultural unincorporated enterprises.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Anaemia Mukt Bharat, launched in 2018, aims to reduce anaemia among
opts: children below five years of age in rural areas only
pregnant and lactating women in urban areas only
elderly persons living alone in all districts
questions.why: The programme targets children, adolescents and women, using supplements, deworming, testing and diet measures.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Which of the following is a marker of the body’s iron stores that is measured in nutrition surveys?
questions.why: Ferritin reflects iron stores in the body and is adjusted for inflammation in nutrition surveys.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Under the Mining Plan and Mine Closure Guidelines 2026 for coal, an operator must
opts: pay the entire closure cost to the State government in advance at the time of lease grant
complete all restoration work before production from the mine is allowed to begin
hand over the mined-out land to the local municipality free of any conditions
open a closure escrow account in a scheduled commercial bank and deposit money each year
questions.why: The guidelines require an escrow account with annual deposits, and withdrawals are checked by the Coal Controller.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Underground coal gasification refers to
opts: washing coal in water to reduce its ash content before sale
crushing coal into fine powder before it is burnt in boilers
converting coal in place into gas that is brought to the surface
storing coal underground in sealed chambers as a national reserve
questions.why: In underground coal gasification the coal seam is burnt in place and the gas produced is brought to the surface.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Which one of the following is an EU measure that charges carbon-intensive imports?
questions.why: The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism puts a carbon price on imports of selected carbon-intensive goods and is a concern in India–EU trade talks.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Negotiations for the India–European Union free trade agreement were concluded on
questions.why: The negotiations were concluded on 27 January 2026, with signing expected in December 2026.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Under the monetary policy framework of India, the inflation target is
opts: 6% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%
3% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 3%
5% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 1.5%
4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%
questions.why: The target is 4% with a band of 2% to 6%. If inflation stays outside the band for three consecutive quarters, the Reserve Bank must report to the government.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An increase in the repo rate makes bank credit costlier.
2. The repo rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank borrows from banks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: A higher repo rate makes credit costlier. The repo rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank lends to banks; the rate at which it borrows is the reverse repo rate.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q: Which one of the following festivals is observed on Karthika Purnima?
questions.why: Guru Nanak Jayanti, the birth anniversary of the first Sikh Guru, falls on Karthika Purnima, which was 24 November in 2026.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q: Guru Tegh Bahadur, whose martyrdom day is observed on 24 November, was the
opts: tenth Sikh Guru, killed at Chamkaur in 1705
fifth Sikh Guru, who compiled the Adi Granth
ninth Sikh Guru, executed in Delhi in 1675
seventh Sikh Guru, who defended Amritsar against Mughal forces
questions.why: Guru Tegh Bahadur was the ninth Guru and was executed in Delhi in 1675 for defending freedom of belief.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q: The Sikh practice of community kitchen that serves free meals to all without distinction is called
questions.why: Langar is the community kitchen, started by Guru Nanak and expanded by later Gurus.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: In the context of public procurement preference for domestic manufacturers, ‘domestic value addition’ refers to
opts: the share of a product’s value created within India
the total import duty paid on the components of a product
the profit margin earned by the seller on each unit sold
the number of workers employed in the final assembly plant
questions.why: Domestic value addition is the portion of a product’s value that is created in India and decides eligibility for purchase preference.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following IT hardware products are covered by the revised domestic value addition methodology announced in November 2026?
1. Laptops
2. Servers
3. Interactive flat-panel displays
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.why: The six product groups are desktop and all-in-one computers, laptops, thin clients, servers, monitors and interactive flat-panel displays.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Insurance Ombudsman is a body that
opts: fixes the premium that every insurer must charge for health policies
grants licences to new insurance companies and agents in each state
resolves complaints of policyholders against insurers
audits the accounts of insurers on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General
questions.why: The Insurance Ombudsman is a grievance-redress authority for complaints against insurers.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Under Section 41(3) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, land acquisition in Scheduled Areas requires the prior consent of
opts: the Governor of the State acting on the advice of the Tribes Advisory Council
the Gram Sabha or the Panchayat or autonomous district council concerned
the Ministry of Tribal Affairs after a public hearing in the district
the District Collector with the approval of the State Legislature
questions.why: The Court has held that prior Gram Sabha consent is mandatory in Scheduled Areas, even in urgency cases.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: For acquisition of land for a private company under the 2013 land acquisition law, the prior consent of at least what share of the affected families is required?
questions.why: A private-company acquisition needs the prior consent of at least 80% of the affected families; for public–private partnership projects the share is 70%.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996
opts: abolishes the Fifth Schedule and extends the Sixth Schedule to all tribal areas
applies to the north-eastern states covered by the Sixth Schedule only
empowers the State Governor to dissolve the Gram Sabha in tribal areas
gives Gram Sabhas in tribal areas powers over natural resources and land
questions.why: PESA extends the Panchayat system to Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule and strengthens the role of the Gram Sabha.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
opts: permits the private sale of all psychotropic substances without any licence at all
applies only to drugs that are produced inside the territory of India itself
prohibits production and sale of narcotics except for medical and scientific purposes
treats every person who uses a drug as guilty of a serious and non-bailable offence
questions.why: The Act controls narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances and allows them only for medical and scientific purposes under licence.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 differs from the earlier Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973 in that it
opts: makes every foreign exchange violation punishable by a prison term
treats most violations as civil offences
bans all transactions in foreign currency by private persons
gives the Enforcement Directorate sole control over exchange rates
questions.why: FEMA replaced FERA and treats most foreign exchange violations as civil, not criminal, offences.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to international courts, consider the following statements:
1. The International Court of Justice settles disputes between states.
2. The International Criminal Court tries individuals for genocide and war crimes.
3. India is a party to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: The ICJ decides disputes between states and the ICC tries individuals. India is not a party to the Rome Statute.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya in a case brought under the
opts: Refugee Convention, 1951 on the status of refugees
Rome Statute, 1998 of the International Criminal Court
Geneva Convention, 1949 on the laws of war
questions.why: The Gambia brought the case under the Genocide Convention and the Court found Myanmar responsible for genocide in the 2017 operations.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Non-Aligned Movement was formally founded in 1961 at
questions.why: The first Non-Aligned Movement summit was held at Belgrade in 1961. The Bandung Conference of 1955 was a forerunner.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Panchsheel, the five principles of peaceful coexistence, was agreed between India and China in
questions.why: The Panchsheel agreement on trade and intercourse with Tibet was signed in 1954.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: In India, the term ‘sum insured’ in a health insurance policy refers to
opts: the maximum amount payable for claims in a policy year
the premium paid by the policyholder each year
the amount charged by a hospital for a day of stay
the discount offered by a network hospital to the insurer
questions.why: The sum insured is the coverage limit of the policy.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about poliomyelitis:
1. India was certified polio-free by the World Health Organization in 2014.
2. Circulating variant poliovirus can arise from the weakened virus in the oral vaccine in under-immunised communities.
3. Wild poliovirus is still reported in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India was certified polio-free in March 2014.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Acute flaccid paralysis surveillance is used to
opts: measure the number of children who have received every routine vaccine
identify children with malnutrition in anganwadi centres across a district
record deaths caused by road accidents in a month in each state
detect cases of polio by investigating sudden limb weakness in children
questions.why: Cases of sudden limb weakness are investigated and tested to detect polio.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) is
opts: a health insurance card that gives every citizen a cover of five lakh rupees
a digital health ID that links a person’s health records with consent
a savings account in which the Government deposits money for medical care
a registry that lists every doctor and hospital in the country by name
questions.why: ABHA is a health account number for consent-based linking of health records. It does not by itself make a person eligible for AB PM-JAY.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The National Cancer Grid is
opts: a network of cancer centres, research institutions and patient groups
a satellite network that monitors the spread of cancer cases across the whole country
a power grid that supplies electricity to radiotherapy machines in district hospitals
a tax scheme that funds the treatment of cancer through a special cess on tobacco
questions.why: The National Cancer Grid is a network of cancer hospitals, research institutions and patient groups across India.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which one of the following best explains how rainfall triggers landslides on a slope?
opts: Rainwater makes the soil lighter so that it floats away down the slope in large masses
Rainwater cools the rock and causes it to expand and then slide down the hillside quickly
Rainwater increases the friction between the soil grains at the base of the slope on a hill
Rainwater raises the pore-water pressure in the soil and reduces its resistance to sliding
questions.why: Higher pore-water pressure reduces the effective stress between soil particles and lowers resistance to sliding.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following describes the Eastern Ghats?
opts: A continuous range that runs along the entire west coast
A mountain range that forms the northern boundary of the peninsula
A discontinuous range of hills along the east coast of India
A volcanic range found only in the north-eastern states
questions.why: The Eastern Ghats are a discontinuous range of hills along the east coast, broken by rivers such as the Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: In disaster risk assessment, ‘exposure’ refers to
opts: how likely a hillside is to fail under heavy and continuous rainfall in a season
what lies in the path of a hazard, such as people, roads and buildings
how badly people and property are affected after a disaster has already taken place
the amount of money that is paid as relief to the affected families in the district
questions.why: Susceptibility, exposure and vulnerability are the distinct parts of risk. Exposure covers the people and property that a hazard could affect.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Which one of the following pathogens is typically handled in a Biosafety Level-4 laboratory?
questions.why: BSL-4 is the highest containment level and is used for dangerous agents with no or limited treatment, such as Ebola and Nipah viruses.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The ‘One Health’ approach recognises that
opts: human health depends only on the quality of hospitals and the supply of medicines
animal diseases can never be passed on to human beings under any circumstances
environmental change has no effect on the spread of infectious disease in a region
the health of humans, animals and the environment is closely linked
questions.why: One Health treats human, animal and environmental health together because many diseases pass between animals and humans.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following ports:
1. Kamarajar
2. Paradip
3. Mundra
4. Deendayal (Kandla)
How many of the above are major ports under the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021?
questions.why: Kamarajar, Paradip and Deendayal are among the 12 major ports under the central government. Mundra is a non-major port in Gujarat.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The second container terminal at Kamarajar Port is to be built on a DBFOT basis. In public–private partnership projects, DBFOT stands for
opts: Develop, Buy, Finance, Own and Transfer
Develop, Build, Finance, Own and Trade
Design, Borrow, Fund, Operate and Transfer
Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer
questions.why: In the DBFOT model the private partner designs, builds, finances and operates the asset for a fixed period and then transfers it to the public authority.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The polyvalent antivenom used across India can be less effective against bites of some pit vipers of the North East.
Statement-II: Venom composition differs between snake species and regions, and an antivenom works best against the venoms it was raised against.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The national antivenom is raised against four common species. Because venom proteins differ among species, it binds poorly to some North-East pit viper venoms.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Which one of the following snakes is among the ‘Big Four’ against which the polyvalent antivenom in India is made?
questions.why: The Big Four are the Indian cobra, common krait, Russell’s viper and saw-scaled viper, which cause most snakebite deaths.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to antivenom, consider the following statements:
1. Polyvalent antivenom in India is made against the venoms of all venomous snakes found in the country.
2. Antivenom is usually made from antibodies raised in animals immunised with venom.
3. Snakebite envenoming is recognised as a neglected tropical disease.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Antivenom is made from antibodies of immunised animals, and snakebite envenoming is on the neglected tropical diseases list. The Indian product covers only the Big Four, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Kashi Tamil Sangamam, consider the following statements:
1. Its first edition was held in 2022.
2. It is organised by the Ministry of Education, with IIT Madras and Banaras Hindu University as implementing partners.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Sangamam began in 2022 and is organised by the Ministry of Education, with IIT Madras and Banaras Hindu University as partners.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Consider the Thirukkural, a classical Tamil work in three parts. The part called ‘Porul’ mainly deals with
opts: liberation and the giving up of worldly life
questions.why: The Thirukkural has three parts: Aram on virtue, Porul on wealth and polity, and Inbam on love.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q:
Consider the following languages:
1. Tamil
2. Marathi
3. Odia
4. Assamese
How many of the above have been given classical language status?
questions.why: Tamil got the status in 2004, Odia in 2014, and Marathi and Assamese in 2024.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021, consider the following statements:
1. It replaced the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963.
2. It empowers the board of a major port authority to fix the scale of rates for its services.
3. It transfers the administration of major ports to the State governments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The 2021 Act replaced the 1963 law and gave port boards more autonomy, including rate-setting. Major ports remain under the Union government.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to pit vipers, consider the following statements:
1. They have a heat-sensing pit between the eye and the nostril.
2. They are non-venomous snakes that kill prey by constriction.
3. Pope’s pit viper is found in the North East of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Pit vipers are venomous and sense the heat of warm-blooded prey through a pit organ. They do not kill by constriction.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In the context of ports, ‘TEU’ is a unit that is used to measure
opts: the cargo-carrying capacity of a ship in tonnes
the water depth of a harbour channel in metres
the berth length available to container ships
questions.why: TEU means twenty-foot equivalent unit, the standard measure of container volume and port capacity.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Constitution Day in India, consider the following statements:
1. It is observed on 26 November to mark the adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly.
2. The Government notified its yearly observance in 2015, the year of the 125th birth anniversary of B. R. Ambedkar.
3. The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949, the yearly observance was notified in 2015, and it came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Who among the following chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.why: Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Assembly and B. N. Rau served as its constitutional adviser.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following languages:
1. Konkani
2. Santhali
3. Tulu
4. Rajbanshi
How many of the above are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.why: Konkani and Santhali are in the Eighth Schedule. Tulu and Rajbanshi are not listed.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. English is one of the languages listed in it.
2. Article 351 directs the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language.
3. The Constitution does not lay down fixed criteria for adding a language to it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: English is not in the Schedule. Article 351 deals with the spread of Hindi, and no fixed criteria for inclusion exist in the Constitution.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A geographical indication is a form of intellectual property linked to the place of origin of goods.
Statement-II: Under the Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999, a registration is valid permanently and never needs renewal.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: A GI links a product’s quality to its place of origin. A registration is valid for 10 years and can be renewed, so the second statement is wrong.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Geographical Indications Registry, which registers GI tags in India, is based at
questions.why: The Geographical Indications Registry functions from Chennai under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Viability gap funding is intended to
opts: lower the interest paid on loans to farmers
support projects that are useful but not financially viable alone
pay the salaries of government staff in new projects
cover the losses of public sector banks every year
questions.why: Viability gap funding is a grant that makes economically useful infrastructure projects financially workable for investors.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following words:
1. Socialist
2. Secular
3. Integrity
How many of the above were part of the Preamble as adopted in 1949?
questions.why: All three words were inserted into the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the making of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. The Constituent Assembly took about 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to complete its work.
2. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly.
3. The Fundamental Duties formed part of the original Constitution of 1949.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The first two statements are accurate. Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Operation Flood, associated with Verghese Kurien, was a programme for
questions.why: Operation Flood was a national programme to build dairy cooperatives and raise milk output.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the amendment of the Indian Constitution under Article 368, consider the following statements:
1. A Bill for amendment can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
2. It must be passed by a majority of the total membership of each House and by two-thirds of the members present and voting.
3. The President may withhold assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill that has been duly passed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: An amendment Bill may start in either House and needs both the total-membership majority and the two-thirds majority of those voting. The President must give assent to it, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The freeze on the inter-State re-allocation of Lok Sabha seats, first imposed by the 42nd Amendment, was extended until the first Census after 2026 by the
questions.why: The 42nd Amendment froze the allocation of seats on the 1971 Census till 2000. The 84th Amendment Act, 2001 extended the freeze to the first Census taken after 2026.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The 106th Constitution Amendment reserves one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
Statement-II: The same Amendment reserves one-third of seats for women in the Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The 2023 Amendment applies the reservation to the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly. The Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils are not covered.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Under Article 368, ratification by the legislatures of at least half of the States is required to amend the provisions on which of the following?
1. Representation of States in Parliament
2. Abolition of a Legislative Council in a State
3. Extent of the executive power of the States
How many of the above require such ratification?
questions.why: Representation of States in Parliament and the extent of the executive power of the States fall under the entrenched list. A Legislative Council is abolished by Parliament under Article 169 through an ordinary law.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to G.V. Mavalankar, consider the following statements:
1. He was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
2. He was elected President of the Constituent Assembly in 1946.
3. He held the office of Speaker until his death in 1956.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Mavalankar became the first Lok Sabha Speaker in 1952 and held the post until he died in 1956. Rajendra Prasad, not Mavalankar, was elected President of the Constituent Assembly in 1946.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. The Speaker is elected by the members of the House from among themselves.
2. The Speaker resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker.
3. The Speaker decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Speaker is elected by the House, resigns in writing to the Deputy Speaker under Article 94, and gives the final certificate on whether a Bill is a Money Bill.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Adaptation Fund was set up under the Kyoto Protocol and now also serves the Paris Agreement.
Statement-II: Its original main income came from a 2% share of the proceeds of Clean Development Mechanism credits.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct. The fund was created under the Kyoto Protocol and funded by a share of credit proceeds, but that income source does not explain why it now serves the Paris Agreement.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: In the context of international climate finance under the UNFCCC process, the Adaptation Fund primarily finances
opts: emission cuts in industrialised countries with high carbon use
compensation for the historical emissions of rich countries
research on solar geoengineering in the polar regions
adaptation projects in vulnerable developing countries
questions.why: The fund pays for concrete adaptation projects and programmes in developing countries that are particularly vulnerable to climate change.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Adaptation Fund
2. Clean Development Mechanism
3. Green Climate Fund
4. Joint Implementation
How many of the above were created under the Kyoto Protocol framework?
questions.why: The Adaptation Fund, the Clean Development Mechanism and Joint Implementation arose from the Kyoto Protocol. The Green Climate Fund was set up under the Convention at the 2010 Cancun conference.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Union Budget, consider the following statements:
1. The Annual Financial Statement is laid before Parliament under Article 112.
2. Money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without an Appropriation Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Article 112 requires the Annual Financial Statement. Article 114 bars withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund except under an Appropriation Act.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following documents presented to Parliament around the Budget:
1. Macro-economic Framework Statement
2. Medium-term Expenditure Framework Statement
3. Economic Survey
How many of the above are required to be laid by the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act?
questions.why: The FRBM Act requires the macro-economic framework and medium-term expenditure statements. The Economic Survey is presented by convention and is not a statutory requirement.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Budget process in Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. Demands for grants are voted only in the Lok Sabha.
2. Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund is not put to vote but can be discussed.
3. The Rajya Sabha can reject an Appropriation Bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Only the Lok Sabha votes on demands, and charged expenditure is discussed but not voted. The Rajya Sabha can only return an Appropriation Bill with recommendations within fourteen days.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Delimitation Commission in India, consider the following statements:
1. Its orders have the force of law and cannot be questioned before any court.
2. Its chairperson is the Chief Election Commissioner of India.
3. Neither House of Parliament can modify its orders.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Orders of the Commission are final and cannot be changed by Parliament. Its chairperson is a retired Supreme Court judge, not the Chief Election Commissioner.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Readjustment of the allocation of seats in the House of the People after each Census is provided for in
questions.why: Article 82 provides for readjustment of seats in the Lok Sabha after each Census. Article 170 does the same for State Legislative Assemblies.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: With reference to the sessions of the Indian Parliament, the power to prorogue a House is exercised by
opts: the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
questions.why: Article 85 empowers the President to prorogue either House. Adjournment sine die is done by the presiding officer, which does not end the session formally.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The allocation of Lok Sabha seats among States still rests on the 1971 Census.
Statement-II: The freeze was meant to ensure that States which controlled population growth did not lose representation.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The freeze on inter-State allocation, imposed in 1976 and extended in 2001, was intended to reward States that succeeded in stabilising population, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the new greenfield airport at Doloo near Silchar in Assam, consider the following statements:
1. The Airports Authority of India will build it.
2. It was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
3. A greenfield airport means an existing airport whose terminal is being expanded.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Authority will build the airport, and the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs cleared it at Rs 2,014 crore. A greenfield airport is built on fresh land, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the scheme approved for the construction and infrastructure equipment industry, consider the following statements:
1. The Ministry of Commerce will implement it.
2. Incentives are graded from 13 per cent to 8 per cent of incremental sales.
3. Viability gap funding of up to Rs 375 crore is meant for a testing facility.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Ministry of Heavy Industries is the implementing ministry, so statement 1 is wrong. The graded sales-linked incentive and the grant of up to Rs 375 crore for a testing facility are both features of the scheme.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Postal Operations Scheme continued for 2026-27 to 2030-31, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme funded by the Union Government.
2. Mail network optimisation is its largest component.
3. One of its components covers philately operations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is a Central Sector Scheme of the Department of Posts with Rs 1,141 crore. Mail network optimisation gets Rs 575 crore, the largest share, and philately operations get Rs 60 crore.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Indian Ocean Rim Association, consider the following statements:
1. India chairs the association for 2025-27.
2. Its secretariat is located in Colombo.
3. India links its chairship to the MAHASAGAR vision.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India holds the chair for 2025-27 and ties it to MAHASAGAR. The secretariat is at Ebene in Mauritius, not Colombo.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the investigation on excess manufacturing capacity in 14 economies, consider the following statements:
1. It is held under Section 301 of the United States Trade Act of 1974.
2. The investigation is conducted by the Dispute Settlement Body of the World Trade Organization.
3. India has told the investigators that it has no structural excess capacity in any sector.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Section 301 is a United States law, and the investigation is carried out by the United States Trade Representative, not by the World Trade Organization. India's Department of Commerce has stated that India has no structural excess capacity.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to bail under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, consider the following statements:
1. Section 43D(5) makes bail harder if the accusation appears prima facie true.
2. Section 43D(2) allows detention before the charge-sheet to be extended beyond the limit under the ordinary criminal procedure law.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Both statements are correct: Section 43D(5) restricts bail where the accusation appears prima facie true, and Section 43D(2) allows longer custody and a longer period of detention before the charge-sheet.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Reserve Bank's November Bulletin article on imported inflation, consider the following statements:
1. Imported items have a weight of about 18 per cent in the new consumer price index basket.
2. Imported items contributed about 18 per cent of headline inflation in October 2026.
3. The new consumer price index uses 2024 as its base year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Imported items form about 8.5 per cent of the new basket but contributed about 18 per cent of October inflation. The new series has the base 2024=100.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.q:
With reference to the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, consider the following statements:
1. It is observed on 25 November and opens the 16 Days of Activism campaign.
2. The campaign ends on 10 December, which is International Human Rights Day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Day falls on 25 November and begins the 16 Days campaign, which closes on Human Rights Day, 10 December.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Red Sea region, consider the following statements:
1. Hodeidah is a port of Yemen.
2. The Bab-el-Mandeb strait links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.
3. The Bab-el-Mandeb strait lies between Oman and Iran.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Hodeidah is a Yemeni Red Sea port and Bab-el-Mandeb joins the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. The strait lies between Yemen on the Arabian side and Djibouti and Eritrea in Africa, not between Oman and Iran.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following groupings:
1. Indian Ocean Rim Association
2. Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation
3. Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
4. Association of Southeast Asian Nations
India is a member of how many of the above?
questions.why: India is a member of the first three. It is a dialogue partner, not a member, of ASEAN.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following ports:
1. Hodeidah
2. Jeddah
3. Kamarajar
How many of the above lie on the coast of the Red Sea?
questions.why: Hodeidah in Yemen and Jeddah in Saudi Arabia are Red Sea ports. Kamarajar is on the Bay of Bengal coast of Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Australia
2. Madagascar
3. Tanzania
4. Thailand
How many of the above are members of the Indian Ocean Rim Association?
questions.why: All four are among the 23 members of the association.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A new airport is being built at Doloo for Silchar rather than expanding the present airport.
Statement-II: The present Silchar airport is a civil enclave on defence land and has little room to expand.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The present airport works inside a defence-owned area, so it cannot grow, and this is why a separate greenfield airport is being built.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The incentive under the construction equipment scheme is linked to incremental sales.
Statement-II: The scheme offers viability gap funding of up to Rs 375 crore for a testing facility.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are features of the scheme, but the testing grant is a separate component and does not explain why incentives are tied to sales.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Section 301 is a provision of the World Trade Organization rules.
Statement-II: Section 301 is a provision of the United States Trade Act of 1974.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Section 301 belongs to the domestic trade law of the United States and is not a World Trade Organization rule.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: With reference to the scheme for the construction and infrastructure equipment manufacturing ecosystem approved for eight years from 2026-27, which one of the following ministries will implement it?
opts: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
questions.why: The scheme is run by the Ministry of Heavy Industries, with Rs 11,000 crore for incentives and a testing facility.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: In the context of the Rs 2,014 crore greenfield airport approved at Doloo in Silchar, the agency that will build it is the
questions.why: The Airports Authority of India is the implementing agency. The other bodies are regulators.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.q: The United Nations General Assembly designated 25 November as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women in the year
questions.why: The Assembly adopted the decision in 1999 and the date recalls the Mirabal sisters of the Dominican Republic, who were murdered in 1960.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: In the Indian Ocean Rim Association, the body that reviews how decisions of the ministers are carried out and coordinates its work programmes is the
opts: Working Group on Trade and Investment
questions.why: The Committee of Senior Officials meets before the ministers to review implementation and work programmes.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Which provision of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act restricts the grant of bail when the accusation appears prima facie true?
questions.why: Section 43D(5) sets the stricter bail condition under the Act. Section 43D(2) deals with police custody, Section 18 with conspiracy and Section 13 with punishment for unlawful activity.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Adjudicating Authority under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, consider the following statements:
1. Its Chairperson must necessarily be a judicial member.
2. Its orders are appealable before the Appellate Tribunal.
3. A judicial member must be on the bench that confirms a provisional attachment, as held by the Supreme Court in November 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Court held that a judicial member must confirm attachments, but the Chairperson need not be one. Appeals from the Authority lie to the Appellate Tribunal.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the disqualification of convicted legislators in India, consider the following statements:
1. Article 102(1)(e) allows disqualification of members of Parliament by a law made by Parliament.
2. Disqualification under Section 8(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 begins only after all appeals are exhausted.
3. A stay of the conviction, and not merely of the sentence, can suspend the disqualification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Disqualification under Section 8(3) takes effect on conviction with a sentence of two years or more, not after appeals. Only a stay of the conviction suspends it.

questions.subject: Agriculture
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. National Milk Day is observed on the birth anniversary of Verghese Kurien.
2. Operation Flood was launched in 1970.
3. Operation Flood was implemented by the National Dairy Development Board.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Verghese Kurien was born on 26 November 1921. Operation Flood began in 1970 under the National Dairy Development Board.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.q:
With reference to the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, consider the following statements:
1. A marriage in violation of the minimum age is void from the start in every case.
2. Child Marriage Prohibition Officers are appointed to prevent such marriages and protect victims.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Under the 2006 Act such marriages are voidable at the option of the child party, not void in every case. The Act provides for Child Marriage Prohibition Officers.

questions.subject: Agriculture
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rice and maize are kharif crops.
2. Wheat is a kharif crop.
3. Crop cutting experiments are used to arrive at yield estimates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Rice and maize are kharif crops, while wheat is a rabi crop. Yield estimates are based on sample harvests known as crop cutting experiments.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to official statistics in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Census of India is conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
2. The Periodic Labour Force Survey is carried out by the National Statistics Office.
3. The National Statistics Office functions under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Census is conducted by the Registrar General under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The National Statistics Office, under the Statistics Ministry, runs the labour force survey.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India–UAE relations, consider the following statements:
1. A Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement between the two countries has been in force since 2022.
2. The Joint Defence Cooperation Committee is chaired by the Defence Ministers of the two countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The trade agreement came into force in May 2022. The Joint Defence Cooperation Committee meets at the level of the Defence Secretary and a senior UAE defence official, not the ministers.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the IndiaAI Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It was approved by the Union Cabinet in 2024 with an outlay of more than ₹10,000 crore.
2. A foundation model is trained for one narrow task and cannot be adapted to others.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Mission was approved in March 2024 with an outlay above ₹10,000 crore. A foundation model is a broad pre-trained model that can be adapted to many tasks.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following areas:
1. Maritime safety and security
2. Cyber security and protection of critical infrastructure
3. Humanitarian assistance and disaster relief
4. Climate finance
How many of the above are among the five pillars of cooperation of the Colombo Security Conclave?
questions.why: Maritime safety and security, cyber security and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief are three of the five pillars; the other two are countering terrorism and radicalisation, and fighting trafficking and organised crime. Climate finance is not a pillar.

questions.subject: Agriculture
questions.q:
Consider the following crops:
1. Rice
2. Wheat
3. Mustard
4. Soyabean
How many of the above are kharif crops?
questions.why: Rice and soyabean are sown with the monsoon and are kharif crops. Wheat and mustard are rabi crops.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Periodic Labour Force Survey
2. Annual Survey of Industries
3. Consumer Price Index (Combined)
4. Wholesale Price Index
How many of the above are compiled by the National Statistics Office?
questions.why: The first three are compiled by the National Statistics Office. The Wholesale Price Index is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Commerce Ministry.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Adjudicating Authority under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act:
1. It tries and punishes persons for the offence of money laundering.
2. It decides whether property attached by the Enforcement Directorate is involved in money laundering.
3. Its orders are appealed directly before the Supreme Court.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: The Authority decides on confirmation of attachment of property and does not try offences, which are tried by a Special Court. Its orders go to the Appellate Tribunal, not directly to the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A stay of the sentence alone does not save a convicted legislator from disqualification.
Statement-II: Disqualification under Section 8(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 follows from the conviction itself.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Disqualification flows from the conviction, so only a stay of the conviction suspends it. Statement-II therefore explains Statement-I.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Supreme Court in the Lily Thomas case struck down Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
Statement-II: Section 8(3) disqualifies a person sentenced to imprisonment for two years or more.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Section 8(4) gave sitting legislators time to appeal and was struck down in 2013. Section 8(3) is a separate provision on the sentence, so Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, an appeal against an order of the Adjudicating Authority lies before
questions.why: The Act provides an Appellate Tribunal for orders of the Adjudicating Authority, and a further appeal on questions of law goes to the High Court.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The disqualification of a member of a State Legislative Assembly under a law made by Parliament is provided for in
questions.why: Article 191 lists the disqualifications for membership of a State legislature, including those laid down by a law of Parliament. Article 102 is the corresponding provision for Parliament.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.q: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the minimum age of marriage for a man is
questions.why: The Act sets 18 years for women and 21 years for men.

questions.subject: Agriculture
questions.q: Operation Flood, which created a national milk grid in India, was implemented under the leadership of the
opts: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
questions.why: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 and run by the National Dairy Development Board, which was set up to promote cooperative dairying.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the cash reserve ratio (CRR) in India, consider the following statements:
1. It is expressed as a percentage of a bank’s net demand and time liabilities.
2. Banks earn interest on the balances they keep with the Reserve Bank to meet it.
3. The Reserve Bank prescribes it under Section 42 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: CRR is a share of net demand and time liabilities and is set under Section 42 of the RBI Act. Balances held as CRR earn no interest, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the daily minimum CRR maintenance announced for the fortnight beginning 1 December 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The daily minimum is lowered from 99 per cent to 90 per cent of the prescribed CRR.
2. The average balance over the fortnight must still meet the prescribed CRR.
3. The prescribed CRR rate itself has been cut.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Only the daily floor is lowered, from 99 to 90 per cent; the fortnightly average requirement is unchanged. The CRR rate itself was not changed.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the entry of foreign portfolio investors into commodity derivatives in India, consider the following statements:
1. Commodity derivatives are regulated by SEBI since the merger of the Forward Markets Commission in 2015.
2. Foreign portfolio investors may now hold physically settled non-agricultural contracts through the delivery period.
3. Until now they could access only cash-settled non-agricultural contracts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: SEBI took over commodity derivatives regulation in 2015, and foreign investors had access only to cash-settled non-agricultural contracts. They must exit physically settled positions before the delivery window, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the contempt powers of the Supreme Court of India, consider the following statements:
1. Article 129 declares it a court of record with power to punish its own contempt.
2. Wilful disobedience of a court order is civil contempt under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.
3. Article 144 requires civil and judicial authorities to act in aid of the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Article 129 gives contempt power, the 1971 Act defines wilful disobedience as civil contempt, and Article 144 obliges authorities to assist the Court. All three are correct.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the power sector in India, consider the following statements:
1. Electricity is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule.
2. State Electricity Regulatory Commissions are set up under Article 324 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Electricity is a Concurrent List subject. State regulatory commissions are created under the Electricity Act, 2003, while Article 324 concerns the Election Commission.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q:
With reference to the Hunger Hotspots early-warning report and related concepts, consider the following statements:
1. It is prepared by the Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme.
2. Phase 5 of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification denotes Catastrophe or Famine.
3. The World Food Programme is headquartered in Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The report comes from FAO and WFP, and Phase 5 of the IPC scale is Catastrophe or Famine. WFP has its headquarters in Rome, not Geneva.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Foreign currency assets
2. Gold
3. Foreign direct investment inflows
How many of the above are components of India’s foreign exchange reserves in the weekly reserves data?
questions.why: Reserves comprise foreign currency assets, gold, special drawing rights and the reserve position in the IMF. FDI inflows are a flow in the balance of payments, not a reserve component.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Iran
2. Pakistan
3. Afghanistan
4. Myanmar
How many of the above are members of the Indian Ocean Rim Association?
questions.why: Iran is a member. Pakistan, Afghanistan and Myanmar are not among the 23 members.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following sites:
1. Kuno National Park
2. Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary
3. Ranthambore National Park
How many of the above have been used for Project Cheetah?
questions.why: Cheetahs have been kept at Kuno and Gandhi Sagar, with a third habitat at Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve. Ranthambore is not part of the project.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Lowering the daily minimum CRR gives banks more flexibility in day-to-day cash management.
Statement-II: The fortnightly average CRR must still meet the prescribed level.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The lower daily floor gives flexibility, and the average requirement remains as a separate condition. It does not explain the flexibility.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Foreign portfolio investors may now hold physically settled non-agricultural commodity contracts through the delivery period.
Statement-II: They must close out or transfer such positions before the tender period begins.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Positions must be closed out or transferred before the tender period, so Statement-I is wrong and Statement-II is correct.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q: MAHASAGAR, the vision announced by India in Mauritius in 2025 and guiding its chairship of the Indian Ocean Rim Association, stands for
opts: Maritime and Holistic Alliance for Security and Growth Across Regions
Mutual and Holistic Alliance for Security and Growth Across Regions
Maritime and Holistic Advancement for Stability and Growth Across Regions
Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
questions.why: MAHASAGAR stands for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions. It was announced in Mauritius in March 2025.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q: With reference to the Indian Ocean Rim Association, whose 25th Council of Ministers met in New Delhi, its secretariat is located at
questions.why: The IORA Secretariat is at Ebene Cybercity in Mauritius.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: With reference to the reintroduction of cheetahs in India under Project Cheetah, the species was declared extinct in the country in the year
questions.why: The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952; the last wild animals had been killed in 1947.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: In the context of Project Cheetah, the first batch of cheetahs released at Kuno in September 2022 was brought from
questions.why: Eight cheetahs came from Namibia in 2022; South Africa sent 12 in 2023 and Botswana nine in 2026.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Under Article 82, the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among States stays frozen until the publication of the figures of the first Census taken after the year
questions.why: The 84th Amendment of 2001 froze the allocation until the first Census after 2026; the new Bill proposes to extend the freeze until the year 2051.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the composition of the legislatures in India, consider the following statements:
1. Article 81 provides for the composition of the House of the People.
2. Article 82 provides for readjustment of seats after each Census.
3. Article 170 provides for the composition of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Article 81 deals with the House of the People, Article 82 with readjustment after each Census and Article 170 with the Legislative Assemblies of the States.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following Constitution Amendments:
1. 42nd Amendment
2. 73rd Amendment
3. 84th Amendment
4. 87th Amendment
How many of the above dealt with the freeze or the Census basis for readjustment of Lok Sabha seats?
questions.why: The 42nd froze the allocation until the first Census after 2000, the 84th extended it until the first Census after 2026, and the 87th changed the basis for readjusting seats within States to the 2001 Census. The 73rd concerns Panchayati Raj.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Extending the freeze on seat allocation to 2051 while enlarging the Lok Sabha uniformly would leave each State’s share of seats unchanged.
Statement-II: A uniform percentage rise in the seats of every State keeps their proportions to each other the same.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: If every State’s seats rise by the same percentage, the ratio between States does not change, which is why the share of each State stays the same.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Article 334A of the Constitution, inserted by the 106th Amendment, deals with
opts: reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha
women’s reservation in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies
nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the House
duration of reservation for Scheduled Castes in Legislatures
questions.why: Article 334A provides one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, to take effect after delimitation that follows the first Census after its commencement.

questions.subject: Security
questions.q:
With reference to the Nilgiri-class (Project 17A) frigates of the Indian Navy, consider the following statements:
1. They use a Combined Diesel or Gas propulsion system.
2. They were designed by the Navy’s Warship Design Bureau.
3. They are powered by nuclear reactors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The ships use a diesel engine with a gas turbine (CODOG) and were designed by the Warship Design Bureau. None of them is nuclear-powered.

questions.subject: Security
questions.q: The seventh and final ship of the Project 17A programme, handed over to the Navy by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers in November 2026, is
questions.why: Vindhyagiri completes the delivery of all seven Project 17A ships within 23 months of the first ship, INS Nilgiri, in December 2024.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, the National Disaster Management Authority is chaired by
questions.why: The National Authority is headed by the Prime Minister, and the State Authorities by the Chief Ministers.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to disaster management in India, consider the following statements:
1. Each State constitutes a State Disaster Response Fund under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
2. The Union government contributes a share of the State Disaster Response Fund.
3. The State Disaster Management Authority is headed by the Chief Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Each State has a fund, the Centre contributes a share to it, and the State Authority is headed by the Chief Minister.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to land records in India, consider the following statements:
1. Land and land revenue records are in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule.
2. The Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme promotes a unique land parcel identification number.
3. A pattadar passbook records the ownership of a landholding of a farmer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Land and land revenue records are State subjects. The unique parcel number scheme and the pattadar passbook statements are correct.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Unique Land Parcel Identification Number under the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme consists of
questions.why: Each plot is given a 14-character alphanumeric number so that records, maps and transactions can be linked; it is also called Bhu-Aadhaar.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the State Legislature:
1. The Governor summons the House of a State Legislature to meet.
2. Prorogation of the Assembly by the Governor dissolves it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Under Article 174 the Governor summons and prorogues the House. Prorogation only ends a session; dissolution of the Assembly is a different act.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The University Grants Commission framed regulations on curbing the menace of ragging in higher educational institutions in
questions.why: The 2009 Regulations followed the Raghavan Committee of 2007 and directions of the Supreme Court, and make institutions responsible for preventing ragging.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to air quality in India, consider the following statements:
1. An Air Quality Index between 201 and 300 is classified as ‘poor’.
2. The ‘severe’ category begins at an Air Quality Index of 301.
3. The Commission for Air Quality Management in the National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas was set up by a law of 2021.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: ‘Poor’ is 201 to 300, and the Commission was created by a 2021 law. ‘Very poor’ is 301 to 400 and ‘severe’ begins at 401.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Commission for Air Quality Management in the National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas was constituted under a law enacted in
questions.why: The Commission was set up by a 2021 Act, replacing the earlier authority for the region, to coordinate action on air pollution across States.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Road transport is exclusively a subject of the Union List.
2. Inter-State road transport services run on permits agreed between the transport authorities of the States concerned under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Inter-State services depend on reciprocal arrangements and permits under the Act. Road transport is not exclusively a Union subject.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.q:
With reference to leave for parents in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 provides 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
2. A male central government employee with fewer than two surviving children is entitled to 15 days of paternity leave.
3. A central law makes paternity leave compulsory in the private sector.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The first two statements are correct. No central law makes paternity leave compulsory for private employers.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q: The road map titled “Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal” was announced during the November 2026 visit to India of the Prime Minister of Nepal,
questions.why: Balendra Shah made his first bilateral visit abroad to India and met the Prime Minister on 23 November 2026.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q:
With reference to India–Nepal relations, consider the following statements:
1. The Treaty of Peace and Friendship between the two countries was signed in 1960.
2. India’s Neighbourhood First policy gives priority to relations with its immediate neighbours.
3. Nepal shares a border with five Indian States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Treaty was signed in 1950. Nepal borders Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q: India and Bangladesh signed an extradition treaty in
questions.why: The treaty was signed in 2013 and amended in 2016 to ease the exchange of wanted persons.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Extradition is usually not granted for an offence of a political character.
Statement-II: Most extradition treaties contain an exception for political offences.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
