Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The exception for political offences is a standard clause in extradition treaties, which is the reason such requests are refused in most cases.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Pakistan
2. Saudi Arabia
3. Türkiye
4. Egypt
How many of the above are members of the Makkah Alliance for Defence, the defence pact signed in August 2026?
questions.why: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye signed the pact; Egypt is not a member.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Strait of Hormuz
2. Gulf of Oman
3. Persian Gulf
4. Gulf of Aden
How many of the above water bodies lie along the coast of Yemen?
questions.why: Only the Gulf of Aden touches Yemen. The Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman and the Persian Gulf lie to the north and east of the Arabian Peninsula, away from Yemen’s coast.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman.
2. The Bab-el-Mandeb strait links the Red Sea with the Arabian Sea directly.
3. The Bab-el-Mandeb strait lies between Yemen and Djibouti.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman, and Bab-el-Mandeb lies between Yemen and Djibouti. It joins the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, which then opens to the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q: The nuclear tests carried out by India at Pokhran in May 1998 were conducted under the code name
questions.why: Operation Shakti included tests on 11 and 13 May 1998; the United States imposed sanctions, which were later eased after the dialogue between the two countries.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q:
With reference to India–US relations, consider the following statements:
1. India conducted the Pokhran-II tests in May 1998.
2. President Bill Clinton visited India in 1992.
3. India conducted its first nuclear test at Pokhran in 1974.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Pokhran-II was in May 1998 and the first test in 1974. Clinton visited India in March 2000.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO) is the national space agency of Pakistan.
2. Bangladesh is a member of the Asia-Pacific Space Cooperation Organisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: SUPARCO is Pakistan’s space agency, and the organisation led by China counts Bangladesh and Pakistan among its members.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the global energy situation in 2025–26, consider the following statements:
1. Natural gas was the largest single source of global primary energy in 2025.
2. India is the world’s third-largest primary energy consumer.
3. The Strait of Hormuz carries nearly a fifth of the world’s maritime oil and gas transport.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Oil, at about 33.5 per cent, was the largest source, ahead of coal and gas. The other two statements are correct.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following sources:
1. Coal
2. Natural gas
3. Nuclear energy
4. Hydropower
How many of the above supplied less than 10 per cent of global primary energy in 2025?
questions.why: Nuclear energy supplied 5.2 per cent and hydropower 2.7 per cent. Coal supplied 27.7 per cent and natural gas 25.1 per cent.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q: New Zealand elects its Parliament by
opts: single transferable vote in multi-member seats
preferential voting in single-member seats with run-offs
questions.why: Party votes decide each party’s overall seat share, with constituency seats counted within it.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In New Zealand’s Parliament of 130 seats, a coalition with 65 seats has a majority.
Statement-II: A majority in a House of 130 members requires at least 66 seats.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Half of 130 is 65, so a majority needs 66 seats; the coalition fell short of it by one.
